issues.description: Method parameter mismatch for addGuestStudents: the Problem Statement and UML specify a method addGuestStudents(int, String): void (an int for the number of new guest students and a String reason), but the solution implementation declares public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) — a single-parameter method. This inconsistency means students following the task/UML will implement a two-parameter method (or expect tests to call it) while the provided solution/reference uses a different signature, causing confusion and potential mismatch with automated tests or instructor solutions.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature consistent across artifacts. Option A (preferred to match the specification): change the solution's method to public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason) and (optionally) store or log the reason or otherwise use it so the signature matches the UML and task description. Option B (if the reason parameter was intentionally omitted): update the Problem Statement and UML to specify addGuestStudents(int): void and remove the String reason from descriptions and diagrams so students and the reference implementation agree.
